Definition: clamor, i.e. acclamation of joy or a battle-cry; especially clangor of trumpets, as an alarum
BiblicalUsage: In Scripture, tᵉrûwʻâh is the word for a shout of joy, a battle cry, the sound of trumpets. In Leviticus 23:24, a memorial of blowing of trumpets. That is the sense it carries through all 33 of its occurrences.
TheologicalSignificance: What grips me is that joy that stays silent is not the joy Scripture shows me; God’s people shout because He has done great things. That is why I read the passages around tᵉrûwʻâh slowly, instead of hurrying past.
